## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṅkhapālacariya* (Cp 20) is the twentieth narrative in the *Cariyāpiṭaka*, the canonical collection of verse accounts illustrating the Bodhisatta's cultivation of the perfections (*pāramitā*) [Bareau; SuttaCentral]. In this birth, the Bodhisatta is reborn as Saṅkhapāla, a king of serpents endowed with extraordinary potency, fearful venom, fangs, and a forked tongue [Bareau]. Resolutely determining upon his ascetic observance along the crossroads of a great highway, he undertakes his vows without regard for his own life, illustrating resolve formulated around the "four factors" (*caturo aṅge adhiṭṭhāya*) [Bareau; Lim 2009].

SuttaCentral notes a passage-level parallel within the collection to the *Bhūridattacariya* (Cp 12), another serpent-king narrative sharing thematic and verbal patterns of resolute observance [SuttaCentral; Lim 2009]. DharmaNexus identifies extensive text reuse with the commentary, the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* (9 shared passages, with the longest sequence spanning segments 4.1–5.4) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments by DharmaNexus also detect minor verbal correspondences with the Tibetan translation of the *Buddhacarita* (*sangs rgyas kyi spyod pa zhes bya ba'i snyan ngag chen po*, D4156) [DharmaNexus].
